claim: tools/bus/bus.py passes its own unit selftest, and that selftest is proven able to fail: every plausible regression in its mutation spec, applied one at a time to a copy of the module, is caught
source: 2026-07-25: the selftest found two real defects on first run. cmd_inbox filtered from_lane == lane, which made 8 of the bus's 9 messages permanently undeliverable because lane B had addressed durable notes to lane B. And a torn append ate the FOLLOWING message, because the next write concatenated onto a fragment with no trailing newline. | 2026-07-25 correction: this claim used to read "passes its own 12-check selftest". The count was never checked by the verifier (bus.py selftest exits 0 on all-pass and reports no count) and went false within a day when the selftest reached 35 checks. A claim whose text asserts more than its command checks is the unverifiable wish this ledger exists to reject. The count is now out of the text; what replaced it is a property the mutation harness actually holds. The verifier moved from bus.py selftest to tools/bus/mutation_check.py in the same pass, because the rewritten text asserts the mutation property and selftest never checked it; leaving it would have reproduced the defect being fixed. C-019 still binds the selftest. 2026-07-25, second pass: the harness moved from tools/bus/mutation_check.py to tools/audit/mutate.py --spec bus. It was bus-specific and the same hole existed in tools/refute/refute.py, so one driver now reads specs from tools/audit/mutations/. The mutant is written BESIDE the target rather than in %TEMP%, because refute.py runs verifiers with cwd=ROOT and a temp copy gets a ROOT that does not exist: every case then turns BROKEN and every mutation looks caught for a reason unrelated to the check under test, which is a harness manufacturing its own green. A count was removed from this claim text on 2026-07-25: the verifier requires every mutation in the spec to be applied and caught and now fails an empty spec, but it does not assert how many mutations exist, so a number here would again assert more than the command checks and would go stale the moment the spec grows. That is exactly how the original '12-check selftest' wording went false.

claim: an edit to a past bus row is detectable, is marked on BOTH read paths rather than delivered as authentic, and a merge that drops an earlier line no longer loses an unread message
source: 2026-07-25, found by reading bus.py against block/buzz's signed-event model. Two defects were reproduced as a failing oracle before anything changed. (1) A third party edited a delivered row's body from 'gate is RED, do not ship' to 'gate is GREEN, ship it' and the bus handed lane C the edited text with nothing marking it as altered: a row that does not commit to its content cannot be told apart from one never touched. (2) The read cursor was a positional offset, which assumes no earlier row ever moves; state/bus.jsonl is git-tracked with two writers (tools/bus/bus.py, tools/dolt/client.py), so a hand-resolved merge dropping one line shifted every lane's cursor and delivered NOTHING where an unread message existed. Scope stated in the module docstring and in verify's own output: tamper EVIDENT not tamper proof, authenticates nobody because every lane is the same OS user, and truncation of the newest rows is undetectable from the log alone. 35 checks, up from 12.

claim: bus.py verify exits nonzero on a broken chain and zero on the real log, whose 12 pre-chaining rows it reports as uncovered rather than clean
source: 2026-07-25. A check that finds defects and exits 0 reports rather than enforces, so verify exits 1 on a break. It does NOT fail on the 12 rows that predate chaining, because failing on pre-existing traffic would make the clean state unreachable; --strict is the opt-in for a caller that wants the whole log chained, and it exits 1 today. Guarded by a mutation harness: 18 plausible regressions applied one at a time to a copy of bus.py, all 18 caught by the selftest, 0 survivors. Two earlier survivors were real gaps and were closed: the deletion test planted its own prev instead of going through cmd_send, so it passed even with cmd_send's prev removed; and the canonical wire format had no cross-version oracle, so it now has a pinned golden vector that deliberately omits origin_lane to hold the omit-absent-keys rule.

claim: refute.py distinguishes an empty ledger from a filter that matched nothing, and a verifier that could not run does not read as a pass
source: 2026-07-25. Two exit-0-while-checking-nothing defects in the refutation engine itself, found while registering unrelated bus claims. (1) `refute.py run --only C-019,C-020` printed 'no claims to check. seed state/claims-verify.jsonl first.' and exited 0 against a ledger holding 20 claims, because --only is a substring match and the comma list matched none of them: a caller asking for specific claims and silently getting none was told its claims held. It now exits 2 and names the count and the match rule; an empty ledger stays 0 because a fresh install is not a failure. (2) BROKEN was printed as 'not a pass' and then excluded from the exit code, so a verifier that timed out, named an unknown shell, or carried no command at all read as success to anything binding on the exit code, making breakage the cheapest way to silence this tool. Exit is now REFUTED plus BROKEN, with --allow-broken as a named hatch someone has to type. 15 checks, including the negative cases (the filter must still filter; expect=fail must still invert) and an assertion that the real ledger and results file were not written by the selftest, since a selftest that appended to state/refutations.jsonl would manufacture the evidence the rest of the system trusts.

Each mutation re-breaks one of the two shipped defects or a verdict rule that would let a claim pass without evidence, including a filter that stops filtering, an exit code hardcoded to 0, expect=fail no longer inverting, and a torn ledger line aborting the whole run. That is exactly how the original '12-check selftest' wording went false.

claim: the repo-vs-live skills checker reports clean on a clean pair and excludes a hollow skill from the deployable set, so a pass from it carries information
source: 2026-07-25. The failure this guards against is hooks_exist.py, which reported success having examined zero hooks: a checker that can only report drift carries no more information than one that can only report clean. skills_sync.py's selftest therefore plants an all-clean pair that must NOT fire and a hollow skill that must be excluded from the deployable set, alongside the drift cases. Every case is planted in a temp directory, so this is portable and is wired into the falsifiability job in .github/workflows/ship-gate.yml rather than depending on the live ~/.claude tree.
